title: Missing MYP Mathematics eAssessment Due to Absence
summary: Learn what happens after missing the MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment, including reporting, rescheduling, evidence and certificate consequences.
body_markdown:
If you are **missing the MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment due to absence** , contact your school’s MYP coordinator immediately. The school records the absence and determines whether to request emergency rescheduling, another mitigation measure or entry in a later examination session. You cannot arrange a private make-up examination, and an alternative sitting is not automatic.


Procedures can vary because coordinators must apply current IB rules alongside school attendance and medical-evidence policies. However, the IB, rather than an individual mathematics teacher, controls whether an externally assessed examination may be rescheduled.


### What happens when you miss the examination?


MYP Mathematics is an externally marked, on-screen examination normally lasting **two hours** . Although schools sometimes call the course “Standard Mathematics,” the IB’s current subject listing distinguishes **mathematics** from **extended mathematics** .


If you do not attend, the coordinator normally records you as **absent** . The absence does not automatically become a zero, an estimated mark or a school-arranged make-up test. The next step depends on the reason, timing, available evidence and applicable IB procedure.


Situation Possible response


Sudden illness or emergency Document circumstances and request an authorized measure


Student can sit soon afterward Consider rescheduling within the permitted window


Student cannot complete the session Consider deferral to a later session


Planned holiday or avoidable commitment Absence may remain unresolved


Illness begins during the examination Provide permitted support and report the circumstances


These are possible routes, not guaranteed outcomes. Coordinators must consult the current assessment procedures available through the IB Programme Resource Centre.


### Illness and adverse circumstances


The IB defines **adverse circumstances** as events beyond the student’s or school’s control that affect assessment performance. Examples can include acute illness, injury, bereavement, severe anxiety, exceptionally difficult family circumstances or an event threatening health or safety.


Under the current[IB adverse circumstances policy](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/adverse-circumstances-policy-en.pdf) , possible measures include access arrangements, rescheduling, an alternative venue, deferral and procedures for missing assessment evidence. The appropriate measure depends on the circumstances, and the school must submit the report or request.


For examination rescheduling, the new sitting generally must occur **within 24 hours after the original scheduled date and time** . IB authorization is normally required because examination security must be protected. A school therefore cannot simply administer the same examination several days later.


If rescheduling is impossible, deferral to a future examination session may be considered. Because MYP Mathematics has one externally assessed examination component, students should not assume that a predicted grade or classroom average will replace it.


### What the student should do immediately


Take these steps even if you are uncertain whether the absence qualifies as an emergency:


1. **Contact the MYP coordinator immediately** , preferably before the examination begins.
2. Explain the reason, when it began and whether you could sit within the next 24 hours.
3. Follow instructions concerning medical or other supporting evidence.
4. Remain available in case rapid rescheduling is possible.
5. Do not discuss the examination with students who completed it.
6. Request written confirmation of the recorded absence and proposed action.


A parent or guardian should contact the school if the student is too unwell. Keep medical certificates, hospital records or travel-disruption notices. Late or vague explanations can make it harder to establish that the circumstances were outside the student’s control.


### What the coordinator must determine


The coordinator confirms the student’s condition, records the absence and checks the current session’s procedures. Relevant issues include whether the event was outside the student’s control, whether examination security can be maintained, whether the student can safely sit within the permitted period and what evidence supports the request.


The[2026 MYP general regulations](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/become-an-ib-school/pdfs/myp-2026-general-regulations.pdf) place adverse circumstances within established IB procedures. Coordinators should not promise a make-up sitting or estimated result before obtaining any required authorization.


### Effect on results and the MYP Certificate


Missing Mathematics can affect more than one subject result. Mathematics is a required assessment area for the full **IB MYP Certificate** , and the[IB’s MYP passing criteria](https://ibo.org/about-the-ib/what-it-means-to-be-an-ib-student/recognizing-student-achievement/about-assessment/myp-passing-criteria/) require students to complete the relevant certificate components.


Without a valid Mathematics result, a student may be unable to receive the full certificate in that session, although results for completed subjects may still be issued. A later session may provide a route to complete the requirement, subject to registration rules. Ask the coordinator to distinguish among the full certificate, individual course results and the school’s own completion documentation.


### Preparing after the decision


If an authorized sitting will occur soon, prioritize recovery and practical readiness. Confirm the reporting time, venue, device arrangements and authorized access arrangements in writing.


For a deferred examination, create a sustainable revision plan. The[MYP Standard Mathematics resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics) supports topic review, while the[Standard Mathematics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics/questionbank) provides targeted practice. Students can also review[how MYP Mathematics is assessed](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-mathematics-is-assessed-and-how-to-revise-for-it) and adapt the[30-day MYP eAssessment study plan](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-eassessments-30-day-study-plan) .


### Common mistakes to avoid


Do not assume that informing the mathematics teacher is sufficient. The **MYP coordinator** manages formal communication with the IB. Likewise, a medical certificate supports a request but does not guarantee rescheduling; timing, circumstances and examination security remain important.


### Conclusion


Report an MYP Mathematics eAssessment absence immediately and follow the coordinator’s instructions. Rescheduling, deferral or another measure may be possible, but no replacement result is automatic. If a later sitting is approved, RevisionDojo Study Notes, Questionbank and timed practice can help maintain your skills while the school provides official guidance.
